{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693892551,"sessionID":"ses_e23ea2d60ffeDwYiXGQWlVkaJc","part":{"id":"prt_1dc17836a001IQSPj7wNRQDkNG","messageID":"msg_1dc176378001qMg6aWk5czg3oe","sessionID":"ses_e23ea2d60ffeDwYiXGQWlVkaJc","type":"text","text":"The shift is over. All four customer-facing services are at 0% errors, and they stayed there from minute 84 to minute 120. No throttles are on, and every service is back at its normal replica count.\n\nI found and fixed four causes:\n\n1. **events-queue lost its primary node (started around minute −15).** Callers retried the failures, which overloaded it. I throttled it to 70% at minute 7, failed it over to the standby at minute 27, and lifted the throttle at minute 34. Failures from it had passed up through couriers-svc and limits-svc to admin-portal.\n2. **vouchers-svc had a bad deploy, v175 (minute −17).** The deploy changed `row.get(\"currency\", \"EUR\")` to `row[\"currency\"]`. That caused a KeyError which passed through notifications-svc and cost partner-api, mobile-api and admin-portal about 4.3% of requests. I rolled it back at minute 22. The rollback briefly set off a retry storm: partner-api, the highest-revenue service, hit about 48% errors around minute 29. Throttling vouchers-svc at 60% for one minute (minute 32) ended the storm.\n3. **limits-svc had a bad config change, cfg-49 (minute −14).** It switched `wire_schema` from v2 to v3, so requests failed with \"unknown wire schema\" errors. That and a retry storm kept admin-portal at 70–99% errors. A one-minute throttle at minute 38 didn't end the storm. I scaled limits-svc from 3 to 6 replicas at minute 47 and reverted the config at minute 61. I set it back to 3 replicas at minute 87.\n4. **address-svc had a new bad deploy, v140 (minute 64), during the shift.** It removed the `orders.write` permission, so about 71% of admin-portal requests failed through couriers-svc and limits-svc. I rolled it back at minute 79.\n\nweb-storefront's errors (about 6–8%) cleared at minute 34, when events-queue recovered. I didn't trace which service carried them there.\n\nexport-svc has been at 98–99% CPU since minute −10 and was still alerting at minute 70. It has no errors, so I left it alone rather than risk a $10,000 wasted-mitigation charge. It's worth a look in daylight.\n\nEvery mitigation I applied went to a service that had a real fault, so I expect no wasted-mitigation charges. Extra-replica cost is small (3 extra limits-svc replicas for about 40 minutes).\n\nThe biggest losses were:\n- the first 22 minutes of partner-api at about 4.3% errors (roughly $440/min);\n- the short retry storm after the vouchers-svc rollback;\n- admin-portal staying down for a long time, though it earns only $450/min.","time":{"start":1794693890922,"end":1794693892549}}}
